title: A simple protocol to detect interacting proteins by GST pull down assay coupled with MALDI or LC-MS/MS analysis.
protocol: Inoculate 5 ml of LB broth with ampicillin in a culture vial containing a single colony of BL21 strain of E.coli (transformed with empty pGEX4T-2 or protein of interest cloned in pGEX4T-2).
Incubate overnight at 37°C with shaking at 200 rpm.
Inoculate 1% of the overnight grown culture into 100 ml of LB broth containing ampicillin and incubate at 37°C with shaking until OD600 reaches 0.6.
Induce the culture with 0.3 mM IPTG for 4 hours.
Harvest the cells by centrifugation at 5500 rpm at 4°C for 15 minutes.
Wash the cells twice with 1X PBS.
Resuspend the pellet in protein extraction buffer.
Add lysozyme to a concentration of 1 mg/ml and incubate on ice for 30 minutes, mixing occasionally.
Add Triton X-100 (0.2%) and DNase (5 µg/ml) to the mixture and shake vigorously.
Incubate at 4°C with gentle shaking for 1 hour to solubilize the fusion protein.
Spin at 10,000 rpm for 10 minutes.
Clarify the supernatant by filtration through 0.4 µm filters.
Prepare a 50% slurry of Glutathione Sepharose 4B from 75% slurry.
Spin at 2100 rpm for 5 minutes.
Decant the supernatant carefully and add 10 bed volume of ice cold 1X PBS, mixing well by inverting.
Spin at 2100 rpm for 5 minutes.
Repeat washing step two more times.
Add 1.0 ml of 1X PBS to prepare a final 50% slurry.
Incubate the clarified crude cell lysate expressing GST or GST fusion protein with 50% slurry for 2-4 hours at 4°C with gentle shaking.
Spin at 500 x g for 5 minutes.
Wash the column three times with 10 bed volume of ice cold 1X PBS.
Elute the interacting protein complex by incubating with 1 bed volume of glutathione elution buffer for 15 min at RT.
Spin at 500 x g.
Repeat this step twice.
Collect each elute separately.
Load the elutes from both column containing immobilized GST and GST fusion proteins adjacent to each other on a 10% SDS PAGE gel with appropriate molecular weight marker.
Stain the gel with either silver stain or Comassie.
Excise the protein bands from the gel for further processing.
Wash the gel with sufficient water and place it on a light box to excise the desired bands with a clean scalpel.
Cut the bands into small pieces (1x1 or 2x2mm) and transfer into a microcentrifuge tube containing water.
Store the tube at 4°C until further processing.
Add 200 µl of destaining solution to the gel pieces and keep at 37°C for 30 min with slow shaking.
Discard the destaining solution and repeat the step.
Add 200 µl 100% ACN to the gel pieces and incubate for 10 min with occasional shaking.
Remove ACN from the tube.
Add 100-200 µl of reducing buffer and incubate at 60°C for 1 hr.
Remove the reducing buffer and allow to cool at room temperature.
Add 200 µl of alkylating buffer for 30 min in the dark at room temperature.
Remove and discard alkylating buffer.
Wash the sample by adding 200 µl of destaining solution and incubate at 37°C for 15 minutes.
Discard destaining solution.
Repeat washing step once more.
Shrink gel pieces by adding 50-100 µl of acetonitrile.
Incubate sample for 15 minutes at room temperature until gel pieces become white (translucent).
Carefully remove acetonitrile and allow gel pieces to air dry for 5-10 min.
Add 10 µl of trypsin solution to the tube containing shrunken gel pieces.
Incubate in ice for 10 min to allow gel pieces to swell and absorb the trypsin solution.
If necessary, add additional 10 µl of trypsin solution to fully cover gel pieces.
Add 25 µl of digestion buffer to the tube.
Incubate sample at 37°C for four hours or at 30°C overnight with shaking.
Remove digestion mixture and place in a clean tube.
To further extract peptides, add 10 µl of 0.5% trifluoroacetic acid or 1% formic acid solution to gel pieces.
Incubate for 5 minutes to inactivate trypsin.
Remove extraction solution and add to digestion mixture.
Centrifuge to remove any gel particles.
Transfer supernatant to a fresh eppendorf and store at 4°C.
